annotations.text:
AKSHAR — variations on Kagad (कागद, paper), now with spice

Each variant got restrained, DIFFERENT garnish rather than the same decoration copy-pasted four times — the spice matches each one's own character instead of flattening them together:

• Devanagari edition numerals (०१, ०२...) on every entry — treats the archive as a numbered literary collection
• A pull-quote on every post — one striking line from the poem set larger, breaking the vertical rhythm
• A small hand-drawn pen-stroke flourish (abstract, not a dingbat) at major structural breaks — A and its footer only, to keep it rare

A (ceremonial) got the fullest treatment: flourish dividers + numerals + pull-quote. B (left rail) deliberately did NOT get a flourish — that would undercut its whole point — so its spice is category-colour-coded rules (terracotta/olive/rose) instead. C (deep ink) layered its pull-quote onto the drop cap and dot-rule it already had. D (bloom) kept its bud icons and got a soft, unitalicised pull-quote in dusty rose.

A · ORIGINAL
Centred, cream ground, quiet terracotta accent. The reference point — everything else is a deliberate departure from this.

B · LEFT RAIL
Same palette and type, but left-aligned in a single reading column with a thin vertical rule marking each entry — reads more like a conventional essay/blog page, less like a spotlight.

TRADEOFF: loses some of the original's ceremony; gains familiarity and a denser, more scannable list.

C · DEEP INK
Richer, more saturated warm tones (antique-paper gold, walnut ink), a framed-photograph treatment for images, a drop cap on the post's opening line, and small dot-rule dividers.

TRADEOFF: more ornamented and confident; slightly heavier-feeling than A, best suited to essay-length work.

D · BLOOM
Softer, airier — blush-rose ground, italic serif headings, rounded image corners, a small line-drawn bud mark at top and bottom.

TRADEOFF: the most delicate and specifically poetry-leaning; would read as too soft for essay-heavy or nonfiction writers.
